articles.title: How to Roll Out Claude Approvals Safely: A Policy File Walkthrough
articles.excerpt: On November 23, 2026, Anthropic launched Claude Ship in beta. It is a set of three agents for GitHub pull requests. One reviews the change, one fixes it, and one decides whether it is ready to merge.…
articles.body: On November 23, 2026, Anthropic launched Claude Ship in beta . It is a set of three agents for GitHub pull requests. One reviews the change, one fixes it, and one decides whether it is ready to merge. As TechCrunch noted , AI coding tools already offered code review. The new part is the third agent. Claude Approvals reads a policy file kept in the repository and can post an approving review on its own, which delegates approval authority to an AI agent. That makes the policy file a security control. A careless policy can let a pull request merge when no person other than its author has looked at it. Anthropic's documentation lists the ways this can happen, so you can design around each one.
articles.author: jamilxt

articles.title: Stop Pasting Passwords Into Your AI Coding Agent
articles.excerpt: autologin-mcp is an open-source MCP server that logs your AI agent's browser tab into the app it is testing. The password stays on your machine and never reaches the model. You ask Claude Code to test…
articles.body: autologin-mcp is an open-source MCP server that logs your AI agent's browser tab into the app it is testing. The password stays on your machine and never reaches the model. You ask Claude Code to test the checkout flow on staging. It opens Chrome, clicks through a few pages, and then the app shows a login form: the session has expired. From there, the run goes one of two ways. The agent stops and waits for you, or it asks you for the password. Neither is what you wanted from an autonomous test run. Every workaround leaks the password The obvious fixes all put the password somewhere it does not belong. Paste it into the chat. Everything in the conversation is sent to the model provider. It stays in transcripts and logs, and it can resurface in context summaries.

articles.body: Originally published on ClueTrove . Install llama.cpp with one script, then run a model straight from Hugging Face with llama cli -hf ggml-org/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF. The engine is free and open source under the MIT license. Pick your model with care. Kimi K3 has about 2.8 trillion parameters, so it is not a laptop model. Qwen3.8 includes a 27B dense model under Apache-2.0, which is the realistic starting point for a normal PC. Kimi K2.5 and Qwen3.5 are no longer the newest. This guide summarizes the llama.cpp README and the model cards, read on 20 October 2026. The short answer Install llama.cpp: curl -LsSf https://llama.app/install.sh | sh (macOS and Linux) or irm https://llama.app/install.ps1 | iex (PowerShell). You can also download releases, use Docker or build from source.

articles.title: We checked 30 public Supabase apps built with AI tools. 21 had at least one high-risk hole.
articles.excerpt: In November 2026, researchers reported that more than 24,000 apps built with Lovable had a Supabase database that answered without a login (Techzine). We wanted to know what the problems actually look…
articles.body: In November 2026, researchers reported that more than 24,000 apps built with Lovable had a Supabase database that answered without a login ( Techzine ). We wanted to know what the problems actually look like in the code. So we took 30 public GitHub projects built with AI app builders that use Supabase, 2,328 database tables in total, and read their migration files and server functions with rls-check , a free checker that runs entirely in your browser. We only read code that was already public. We ran nothing, attacked nothing and contacted nobody, and no project is named here. The numbers 21 of 30 projects (70%) have at least one high-risk problem. 7 of 30 have a secret key in their public code : the Supabase master key (service role), a live Stripe secret key, or an AI provider key.

articles.title: Model Routing Is a Policy Decision
articles.excerpt: Originally published at Trida AI. Who chose the model that answered your last production request? If you run a single model, the answer is boring, and boring is good. You chose it, your evals cover it…
articles.body: Originally published at Trida AI . Who chose the model that answered your last production request? If you run a single model, the answer is boring, and boring is good. You chose it, your evals cover it, and a bad answer has one place to look. Add a router and the answer gets murkier. Now a piece of software you did not write predicts, request by request, which model in a family will answer well enough, and sends the work there. The savings are real. So is the thing you gave up: you no longer know, in advance, which system your users are actually talking to. That trade can be worth making. It should be made on purpose. What a managed router actually decides Take the clearest managed version on offer.

articles.title: Your Breast Ultrasound Model's Accuracy Problem Might Be a Labeling Problem
articles.excerpt: When a medical imaging model underperforms, the first instinct is to change the architecture or tune hyperparameters. But in breast ultrasound, the real culprit is often upstream: the labels. Ultrasou…
articles.body: When a medical imaging model underperforms, the first instinct is to change the architecture or tune hyperparameters. But in breast ultrasound, the real culprit is often upstream: the labels. Ultrasound is noisy, operator-dependent, and full of subtle lesion features like irregular margins and posterior shadowing. That makes breast ultrasound annotation harder than most computer vision labeling, and mistakes get baked straight into your model. Here are three quick audits you can run on a dataset before you train. 1. Check inter-rater agreement If two annotators label the same images and often disagree, your ground truth is noisy. For categorical labels (for example benign vs. malignant), Cohen's kappa is a quick check: from sklearn .

articles.title: November’s full moon rises tonight! Here’s how to see the Beaver Moon supermoon
articles.excerpt: A dam good moon.
articles.body: Get ready stargazers! The full "Beaver supermoon" rises in the eastern sky, offering up a spectacular display shortly after sunset tonight (Nov. 24). Here's what you need to know. November's full moon occurs at 9:53 a.m. EST (1453 GMT) on Nov. 24, as the lunar disk passes opposite the sun in our sky, making it appear fully lit from our perspective. The November full moon is often referred to as the Beaver Moon because it rises around the time the small mammals are hard at work building their lodges in preparation for the winter. The Beaver Moon is also set to be a dazzling supermoon , because it turns full as the natural satellite passes within 90% of perigee , when it is at its closest to Earth in its 27-day elliptical orbit.

articles.title: Will astronauts farm on the moon? Scientists successfully grow potatoes in simulated lunar dust
articles.excerpt: Researchers have successfully grown potatoes in simulated lunar regolith, possibly opening the door for farming on future moon bases.
articles.body: It's no secret that NASA is working towards a permanent presence on the moon. The space agency even plans to build a moon base for its astronauts to call home. But humans living inside lunar habitats around the clock will need three square meals a day, so researchers have been working on how to grow food on the moon. To that end, a team from the College of Agricultural Sciences at Oregon State University have been raising potatoes in simulated moon dust with promising results. The researchers published their findings Nov. 20 in the Microgravity science journal.

articles.body: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here . Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing.
